Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — great product. Our legal team has taken a pass at Redwood's standard DPA and attached a redline (BrightBridge_DPA_redlines_v3.pdf). Key asks I want to call out up front to save back-and-forth: 

- Data residency: BrightBridge requires production data for "customer personal data" to be stored only in the United States (we are a US-only-covered entity).
- Retention / deletion: Our standard is that upon contract termination or deletion request, personal data (including backups) must be permanently deleted within 30 days.
- Backups/logs: We expect the vendor to limit backup retention to 30 days. Audit logs can be retained up to 365 days but must be pseudonymized and not linked to PHI.
- Proof of deletion: We need a technical attestation within 45 days of deletion request and an option for a certified third-party deletion report annually.
- KMS & keys: We prefer customer-managed keys (CMK) for any data at rest for PHI; if not available, explicit contractual guardrails for key handling.
- Subprocessors: We need a complete list of subprocessors with 30-day notice for any changes and the right to object.

Can you confirm Redwood can accept these items, or propose alternative language? If helpful, our counsel (legal@brightbridgehealth.com) is copied and can take a direct call next week.

Best,
Emma Jones
Senior Counsel, BrightBridge Health

Vanessa – quick legal read and recommended positions below. High level: we should be collaborative but not concede operationally infeasible SLAs. Proposed counters aim to close the gap while protecting Redwood's multi-tenant hosting obligations.

1) Data residency (prod personal data):
  - For Dedicated and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), accept US-only storage for customer-designated datasets.
  - For Hosted (shared), offer region-level residency (US region) and contractual committal to not transfer data outside the US region except for limited operational reasons (law enforcement, customer-requested exports). We cannot guarantee single-country boundaries for all telemetry/infra-related telemetry.

2) Deletion and backups:
  - Define "deletion" as removal of primary and replica data and cryptographic erasure of associated keys where applicable.
  - Offer 30-day deletion for primary data and a distinction for immutable backups: allow up to 90 days for backups to be pruned to meet restore continuity; provide an attestation of deletion within 45 days after the backup retention window ends.
  - For Hosted customers, note that snapshots in cold-storage and long-term disaster recovery stores may be subject to up to 90 days retention; include a clause for expedited deletion in the case of contractual termination (for an additional compliance fee or under Dedicated/Private contract).

3) Proof of deletion:
  - We can provide internal deletion logs and a signed attestation. Third-party certified deletion reports can be provided annually as part of an audit addendum (billable).

4) KMS & keys:
  - CMK support is available for Dedicated and Private customers. For Hosted, we offer a managed keys option with strict separation and rotation policies; offer a SOC2+KMS attestation and HSM-backed key storage.

5) Subprocessors:
  - We'll provide a current list and 30 days' notice for material changes. Right to object: limited to reasonable security/privacy grounds; failure to resolve after escalation results in termination rights for customer.

6) Logs / telemetry exceptions:
  - Allow pseudonymized/aggregated telemetry for platform health up to 180 days. No PHI in telemetry.

7) Legal hold / regulatory exceptions:
  - Include carve-outs for legal holds and for required retention under statutory obligations.

Action: Vanessa — I'd propose we send a short redline with the concrete alternate wording (I can draft). Keep BrightBridge in the loop and offer a 30-minute call to finalize.

-Marcus

Hi Emma — thanks for the redline and the clarity on BrightBridge's requirements. We've reviewed internally and have a few proposed alternatives that we hope close the gap quickly. I'm attaching a short draft with proposed language, but the key points are below so we can align before a call: 

1) Residency: For Dedicated and Private deployments we can accept US-only residency for customer-designated personal data. For our Hosted product we will commit to US-region residency (data stored in a US region) and to not transfer Personal Data outside the US except as required by law or at your request. We cannot always guarantee country-level isolation for platform operational data (telemetry, infra logs).

2) Deletion & backups: We will commit to deletion of primary data within 30 days of request/termination. For backups and disaster-recovery copies we propose a 90-day maximum retention window to preserve restore capability and system integrity; within 45 days of the backup window ending we will provide a signed attestation that the backups have been pruned. If BrightBridge requires a strict 30-day backup purge, we can offer that for Dedicated/Private deployments or as a premium compliance option for Hosted.

3) Proof of deletion: Redwood will provide internal deletion logs and a signed attestation within 45 days of completion. We can include an annual third-party verification as an addendum.

4) KMS: Customer-managed keys are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted, we offer HSM-backed managed keys and robust key controls; we can discuss further technical mitigations to meet your security team.

5) Subprocessors & notices: We'll provide the current subprocessor list and 30 days' notice for changes. Objection mechanism can be limited to documented security/privacy concerns.

6) Exceptions: We will carve out legal holds and statutory retention obligations. Platform telemetry will be pseudonymized and limited to operational metrics.

If this direction looks ok, Marcus can turn this into specific redline language and we can either send that back or schedule a 30-minute call. What time next week works for you?

Thanks,
